question_text: What must you reckon with here?

options.text: The vehicle in front changing lanes
Denser traffic beyond the underpass
The right-hand lane coming to an end

correct_answers.text: The vehicle in front changing lanes
Denser traffic beyond the underpass

comment: The sign announces the end of the left lane. The traffic flow will condense from two lanes to a single lane. Halting traffic might occur. The vehicle in the left lane will change the lane. You have to allow the vehicles on the left side of the lane to change over to your lane according to the zip merging principle.

question_text: What must you do here?

options.text: Check your speed again and, if necessary, brake
Brake only on the bend so as not to obstruct traffic following behind

correct_answers.text: Check your speed again and, if necessary, brake

comment: If the car driver drives at high speed on the highway for a long time, the senses get used to the fast pace. There is a risk of underestimating the pace. In particular, if you want to drive out, check your speed on the speedometer. Use the deceleration lane of the freeway to reduce your speed. Braking there doesn't hinder anybody. Then you can enter the sharp bend of the exit at a reasonable speed.

question_text: A traffic jam is building up here. What is the correct procedure?

options.text: If possible, switch on hazard warning lights to warn vehicles following behind
Drive as far as possible to the right in order to leave room for a channel on the left
Drive as far as possible to the left in order to leave room for a channel on the right

correct_answers.text: If possible, switch on hazard warning lights to warn vehicles following behind
Drive as far as possible to the right in order to leave room for a channel on the left

comment: If you drive towards a traffic jam, turn on your hazard lights to alert other road users. It is important to build a rescue lane for any approaching rescue vehicles. In this case, drive as far to the right as possible.

question_text: What must you anticipate with inclines on motorways?

options.text: Slow-moving trucks on the right-hand lane
Sudden overtaking manoeuvres by other road users
Large differences in speed between vehicles

correct_answers.text: Slow-moving trucks on the right-hand lane
Sudden overtaking manoeuvres by other road users
Large differences in speed between vehicles

comment: When driving uphill on motorways, you should expect slow-moving trucks in the right lane, sudden overtaking manoeuvres by other road users and large speed differences between vehicles. All 3 answers are correct.

question_text: What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in lane
Move to the left-hand lane
Maintain speed and stay in lane

correct_answers.text: Slow down and stay in lane

comment: Since you are currently being overtaken by a car on the left-hand side, you must maintain the lane and reduce the speed until the truck in front of you has completed its overtaking maneuver and changes to the right-hand lane.

question_text: What must you be aware of when joining the motorway?

options.text: On the merging lane, I may drive faster than the through-driving traffic
The through-driving traffic has priority
The through-driving traffic on the right-hand lane must allow incoming traffic to merge

correct_answers.text: On the merging lane, I may drive faster than the through-driving traffic
The through-driving traffic has priority

comment: On the freeway, the continuous traffic always has the right of way and does not have to allow entrance. On the acceleration lane the driver may drive faster than the rest of the vehicles.

question_text: You are driving at the recommended speed on the motorway and want to leave it at the next exit. What should you do?

options.text: I cease overtaking manoeuvres in good time
I significantly reduce my speed on the exit lane
I significantly reduce my speed while still on the right-hand lane of the motorway

correct_answers.text: I cease overtaking manoeuvres in good time
I significantly reduce my speed on the exit lane

comment: Finish overtaking in good time and get on the right lane. Before changing to the deceleration lane look around and indicate. On the deceleration lane, check your speed on the speedometer in order to assess it right. Only on the deceleration lane you should reduce the speed significantly, so as not to hinder subsequent traffic on the continuous lane.

question_text: After a longer journey travelling at about 120 km/h, you want to exit the motorway. What must you be aware of when doing so?

options.text: I signal in good time and then brake while on the exit lane, so as not to impede the traffic behind me
I check the speedometer to make sure I do not underestimate my speed
I maintain my speed while on the exit lane, so as not to impede the traffic behind me

correct_answers.text: I signal in good time and then brake while on the exit lane, so as not to impede the traffic behind me
I check the speedometer to make sure I do not underestimate my speed

comment: If you, as a car driver, leave the motorway at a speed of about 120 km/h, you must observe the following: 1. complete all overtaking maneuvers in good time; 2. merge right; 3. reduce the speed while checking it on the speedometer; 4. indicate. In order not to hinder the traffic on the continuous road, you should reduce the speed only when you change to the deceleration lane.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: I slow my vehicle down
I switch on my hazard lights
I continue driving in the clear lane

correct_answers.text: I slow my vehicle down
I switch on my hazard lights

comment: When approaching a jam end on the highway, you must reduce your speed and warn the road users behind you by switching on the hazard lights. A rescue lane is to be formed.

question_text: What should you anticipate with this bend?

options.text: With an obstacle situated around the corner
That the bend will become tighter as it progresses
With oncoming traffic on my lane

correct_answers.text: With an obstacle situated around the corner
That the bend will become tighter as it progresses

comment: The course of the curve is not assessable. You always have to expect obstacles such as broken-down vehicles or traffic jams. Be prepared for a stop within sight. The curve may narrow in its course. Thereby you'll only notice in the curve that your speed is too high. It is important to reduce the speed on time.

question_text: What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I have to reduce my speed
The truck has right of way
The truck has to wait

correct_answers.text: I have to reduce my speed
The truck has right of way

comment: The curve is difficult to assess for the car driver. There may be other road users or even obstacles on the route. Therefore, it makes sense to slow down the pace even before the turn and mentally adjust to a possible danger situation. Because even for oncoming drivers this is a difficult spot and caution is required.

question_text: Why do you have to slow here?

options.text: Because of the truck
Because of the speed limit
Because of the white car

correct_answers.text: Because of the truck

comment: The moveable road barrier with flashing arrow in the right-hand lane forces the truck driver to change to your lane on the left. That's why you have to delay now. The white car behind you is no danger.

question_text: Why do you have to reduce your speed now?

options.text: Because of the blue car
Because of the speed limit
Because of the red van

correct_answers.text: Because of the blue car

comment: In this situation, the blue car is likely to change to the right lane. You should therefore reduce your speed and keep a safe distance from it

question_text: You are driving at least 20 km/h faster than the green truck. What should you do?

options.text: I move onto the motorway ahead of the green truck
I brake and move onto the motorway behind the green truck
I stop at the end of the merging lane, and move onto the motorway behind the blue truck

correct_answers.text: I move onto the motorway ahead of the green truck

comment: You are on an acceleration lane to the freeway. On the acceleration lane it is permissible to drive faster than the vehicles on the continuous lane. Therefore, you can drive onto the highway at a faster pace in front of the green truck.

question_text: You are approaching these vehicles. What should you do in this situation?

options.text: I remain on the middle lane but without overtaking the white car
I remain on the middle lane and cautiously overtake the white car
I move into the left-hand lane and flash my headlights until the person in front vacates the lane

correct_answers.text: I remain on the middle lane but without overtaking the white car

comment: The white car on the left lane must not be overtaken on the right. To go behind it on the left lane and to make him/her change with flash light is also prohibited. You have to slow down and drive on the middle lane just as fast as the car. Allow him/her as much distance as it takes in order for him/her to be able to change to the middle lane at any time.

question_text: You are driving a truck. What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I increase the distance to the vehicle ahead
I maintain my speed
I overtake the truck in front of me

correct_answers.text: I increase the distance to the vehicle ahead

comment: Please magnify the distance to the vehicle ahead and therefore hold a required safety distance.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: - do not switch lanes, because [the red car] is already moving across
- move into the middle lane, because my overtaking manoeuvre is complete
- switch lanes so that I do not obstruct [the yellow car]

correct_answers.text: - do not switch lanes, because [the red car] is already moving across

comment: Next to you is a red car that changes into the middle lane. Therefore, you cannot change the lane, otherwise you would endanger other road users.

question_text: You want to join the motorway. What driving line should you follow?
comment: While driving onto the freeway you should continue to follow the third driving line, so stay true to the lane and do not cut the boundary line.

question_text: What should you be prepared for now?

options.text: [The yellow car] exits the motorway
The motorbike exits the motorway
The [blue bus] in front of me brakes due to a traffic jam

correct_answers.text: [The yellow car] exits the motorway

comment: No traffic jam can be seen in this situation. Since the motorcycle is driving on the left, it will not leave the motorway. On the other hand, the car driving on your left flashes to the right. You can be prepared for the driver to leave the motorway.

question_text: You want to exit the motorway. What is creating a dangerous situation here?

options.text: The motorbike
[The yellow truck]
[The green vehicle]

correct_answers.text: The motorbike

comment: The motorbike behind you (see right wing mirror) creates a dangerous situation for you. Take this into account when leaving the motorway.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I remain in the left-hand lane
I continue driving as before

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed
I remain in the left-hand lane

comment: There is an object on the roadway in the right lane in front of the truck. Truck will avoid the object by using the left lane. You should therefore stay in the left lane. If you continue to drive unchanged, you could collide with the truck. You should therefore reduce your speed.

question_text: Why must you reduce your speed now?

options.text: Because of the truck
Because of the speed limit
Because of the [blue] car

correct_answers.text: Because of the truck

comment: The right lane is blocked in front of the truck. He has to change to the left lane. To allow him to do this, you should reduce your speed. The car driving behind you is no reason for you to slow down. The maximum permissible speed here is 120 km/h. Keep this in mind.

question_text: You want to leave the motorway. What is the right course of action?

options.text: I use the speedometer to check my speed at short intervals
I reduce my speed now
I reduce my speed only once I am at the turn

correct_answers.text: I use the speedometer to check my speed at short intervals
I reduce my speed now

comment: As soon as you have entered the deceleration lane, you should brake. If you brake before entering the deceleration lane, you will unnecessarily interfere with traffic on the motorway. You should check your speedometer more often to make sure you are not entering the bend too fast. On motorways, there is a danger that you will get too used to the high speed and therefore enter an exit too fast. If you were to slow down at the turn, you would not be able to reduce your speed in time. In general, you should always brake before a bend and not only in the bend.

question_text: When driving on motorways, why should you maintain the recommended speed of 130 km/h?

options.text: - can prevent accidents occurring
- can reduce the severity of possible accidents
- achieves an even flow of traffic

correct_answers.text: - can prevent accidents occurring
- can reduce the severity of possible accidents
- achieves an even flow of traffic

comment: The higher the speed, the longer the reaction distance, braking distance, etc. If all vehicles travel at a similar speed, the traffic flow becomes more even.

question_text: What must you anticipate here?

options.text: The driver of the [yellow truck] does not notice the start of the tailback in time
The motorbike drives between the lines of vehicles
[The blue car] pulls into my lane in front of me

correct_answers.text: The driver of the [yellow truck] does not notice the start of the tailback in time
The motorbike drives between the lines of vehicles

comment: Due to the sudden traffic jam, the driver of the truck sees the end of the traffic jam too late. Due to the traffic jam, the motorcycle will try to go through the rows of vehicles.

question_text: What should you anticipate when driving out the exit slip road?

options.text: A broken-down vehicle
People on the carriageway
A fallen load

correct_answers.text: A broken-down vehicle
People on the carriageway
A fallen load

comment: A warning triangle indicates a nearby obstacle, e.g. people, a defective vehicle or a fallen load, in the exit lane. Therefore, enter the exit at a very reduced speed.

question_text: Why should you avoid overtaking alongside the roadworks site?

options.text: The time saved is frequently insignificant
Vehicles in the right-hand lane may cross over the yellow road markings
The risk of an accident increases significantly

correct_answers.text: The time saved is frequently insignificant
Vehicles in the right-hand lane may cross over the yellow road markings
The risk of an accident increases significantly

comment:
When overtaking in the construction site area, the risk of accidents is significantly increased, because there is a risk that the vehicles that you want to overtake run over the yellow lane marking. The lanes are mostly narrower and the distractions on the edge of the road can lead to inattentiveness.
Overtaking in the construction site area often saves almost no time, since most drivers in the construction site area only drive the maximum speed.

question_text: How can you reduce the risk of driving onto a motorway against the stipulated direction?

options.text: I deliberately look for traffic signs showing the right direction of travel at motorway slip roads
I pay close attention to the signage when the traffic routing changes
When encountering roadworks, I only follow the information provided by my navigation system

correct_answers.text: I deliberately look for traffic signs showing the right direction of travel at motorway slip roads
I pay close attention to the signage when the traffic routing changes

comment: To avoid driving against the direction of travel on the motorway, you should always pay attention to the relevant traffic signs. It is very important to pay attention to the exact signs, especially when the traffic routing has changed.
